key_insight: Positioning a phononic subsurface beneath a separated flat-plate flow can either amplify or attenuate sustained vortex shedding, with one configuration reducing lift oscillations by over 30% and drag oscillations by over 50%.
engineering_relevance: Passive phononic subsurfaces could reduce oscillatory aerodynamic loads while preserving mean lift and drag.
method: Simulate strongly coupled nonlinear fluid–structure interaction using a high-fidelity immersed boundary method.
Model the phononic subsurface as a grounded diatomic chain driving a compliant plate section.
Vary chordwise position and resonant displacement-amplitude growth; analyze frequencies, phase relationships, and flow fields.
evidence_signal: Simulations identify four position-dependent limit-cycle regimes and a configuration achieving the reported oscillation reductions with less than 0.5% change in mean lift and drag.
watch_item: Performance is position-sensitive, and the abstract provides no experimental validation or evidence of transferability beyond the simulated flat-plate flow.
paper_title: Interaction of Sustained Vortex Shedding with a Phononic Subsurface: Effect of Positioning and Resonant Characteristics
